nodes.name: Definition 4.7, Definition 4.8: Essentiality
nodes.statement:
Let $s$ and $t$ be terms and $\mathcal{U}$ a set of redexes in $s$ such that $s \Rightarrow^\mathcal{U} t$. The map $\varepsilon$ from prefix sets $P$ of $t$ to prefix sets of $s$ is defined as:
\[
\varepsilon_{P}({s \Rightarrow^\mathcal{U} t}) = \zeta(\Psi)
\]
where $\Psi$ is the path prefix set of $P$ with respect to $\mathcal{U}$.

nodes.name: Definition 4.12: Measure
nodes.statement: The \emph{measure} $\mu_{P}({D})$ of $D$ with respect to the prefix set $P$ of $s_n$ is the $n$-tuple $(l_n,\ldots,l_1)$ --- note the reverse order! --- such that $l_i$, with $1 \leq i \leq n$, is the cardinality of the path prefix set of $P_i$ with respect to $\mathcal{U}_i$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.10
nodes.statement: Let $s$ and $t$ be terms, $\mathcal{U}$ a set of redexes in $s$ such that $s \Rightarrow^\mathcal{U} t$, and $P$ a prefix set of $t$. If $p \in \mathcal{P}os(s)$ does not occur in the redex pattern of a redex in $\mathcal{U}$ and is not the position of a variable bound by a redex in $\mathcal{U}$, then $p$ is essential if{f} there exists a position $q \in P$ such that $q \in p/(s \Rightarrow t)$ and $p$ is inessential if{f} no descendant of $p$ occurs in~$P$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.14
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a prefix set of $s_n$ in $D$ and let $t_0$ mirror $s_0$ in the positions essential for $P$ in $s_0$. There exists a finite sequence $E$, with $\mathcal{V}_i$ for all $1 \leq i \leq n$ \emph{finite} and consisting \emph{solely} of essential redexes, such that $E$ mirrors $D$ in $P$ and $\mu_{P}({E}) = \mu_{P}({D})$.

nodes.name: Definition 4.15: Emaciated projection across $\rightarrow$
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a prefix set of $s_n$ in $D$. If $s_0 \rightarrow t_0$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u/D$ occurs at a position in $P$, then the \emph{emaciated projection} of $D$ across $s_0 \rightarrow t_0$ with respect to $P$, written $D \mathord{\sslash} u$, is defined as $E/u$, where $E$ is the result of applying Lemma 4.14 to $D$ with $E$ starting in $s_0$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.16
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a prefix set of $s_n$ in $D$. If $s_0 \rightarrow t_0$ contracts an essential redex $u$ such that no redex in $u/D$ occurs at a position in $P$, then $\mu_{P}({D \mathord{\sslash} u}) \prec \mu_{P}({D})$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.17
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a prefix set of $s_n$ in $D$. If $s_0 \rightarrow t_0$ contracts an inessential redex $u$, then $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ mirrors $D$ in $P$ and $\mu_{P}({D \mathord{\sslash} u}) = \mu_{P}({D})$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.21, Corollary 4.22
nodes.statement:
Let $s$ and $t$ be terms, $\mathcal{U}$ a set of redexes of $s$ such that $s \Rightarrow^\mathcal{U} t$, and $P$ a prefix set of $t$. If $s \Rightarrow^{\mathcal{V}_1} t' \Rightarrow^{\mathcal{V}_2} t$ with $\mathcal{V}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}_2 = \mathcal{U}/(s \Rightarrow t')$, then the set of positions essential for $P$ in $s$ is identical along $s \Rightarrow t$ and $s \Rightarrow t' \Rightarrow t$.

Let $s$ and $t$ be terms, $\mathcal{U}$ a set of redexes of $s$ such that $s \Rightarrow^\mathcal{U} t$, and $P$ a prefix set of $t$. If it holds that:
\begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$]
\item
$s \Rightarrow^{\mathcal{V}_1} s' \Rightarrow^{\mathcal{V}_2} t$ with $\mathcal{V}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}_2 = \mathcal{U}/(s \Rightarrow s')$, and
\item
$s \Rightarrow^{\mathcal{V}'_1} t' \Rightarrow^{\mathcal{V}'_2} t$ with $\mathcal{V}'_1 \subseteq \mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}'_2 = \mathcal{U}/(s \Rightarrow t')$,
\end{enumerate}
then the set of positions essential for $P$ in $s$ is identical along $s \Rightarrow s' \Rightarrow t$ and $s \Rightarrow t' \Rightarrow t$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.25
nodes.statement: Let $D$ and $E$ be finite sequences of complete developments starting in the same term $s$. Moreover, let $P$ be a prefix set of the final term of $D$ and let $E$ mirror $D$ in $P$. If $s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in either $u / D$ or $u / E$ occurs at a position in $P$, then $E \mathord{\sslash} u$ mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ in $P$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.23
nodes.statement:
Let $D: s_0 \Rightarrow s_1 \Rightarrow \cdots \Rightarrow s_n$ and let $P$ be a prefix set of $s_n$. If $s_0 \rightarrow t_0$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u/D$ occurs at a position in $P$ and such that $D/u$ exists, then for every redex $v$ in $s_0$:
\begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$]
\item
if $v$ is essential, then $v$ is either $u$ or there exists a residual of $v$ in $t_0$ that is essential for $P$ along $D/u$, and
\item
if $v$ is inessential, then all residuals of $v$ in $t_0$ are inessential for $P$ along $D/u$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.27
nodes.statement: Let $D$ be a finite sequence of complete developments starting in a term $s$. Moreover, let $P$ and $P'$ be prefix sets of the final term of $D$ such that $P' \subseteq P$. If $s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u / D$ occurs at a position in $P$, then $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P'$ sub-mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.24
nodes.statement:
Let $D : s_0 \Rightarrow s_1 \Rightarrow \cdots \Rightarrow s_n$ and let $P$ be a prefix set of $s_n$. If $s_0 \rightarrow t_0$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u/D$ occurs at a position in $P$, then for every redex $v$ in $s_0$:
\begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$]
\item

if $v$ is essential, then $v$ is either $u$ or there exists a residual of $v$ in $t_0$ that is essential for $P$ along $D \mathord{\sslash} u$, and
\item
if $v$ is inessential, then all residuals of $v$ in $t_0$ are inessential for $P$ along $D \mathord{\sslash} u$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.28
nodes.statement: Let $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow s_\omega$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$. For every $s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0$, redex $u$ in $t_0$, and $d \in \mathbb{N}$ no redex in $u / D_d$ occurs at a position in $P_d$, with $D_d = (s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0)$ with respect to~$P_d$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.15
nodes.statement: If $s$ can be reduced to a normal form by a strongly convergent reduction, then it also reduces to a normal form by any needed-fair reduction. Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.7, Theorem 5.9
nodes.statement:
If $s$ can be reduced to normal form by a strongly convergent
reduction, then it also reduces to a normal form by
any outermost-fair reduction. Any
such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.

If $s$ can be reduced to a normal form by a strongly convergent reduction, then it also reduces to a normal form by any fair reduction. Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.
